005package org.wpilib.command3;
006
007import java.util.List;
008import java.util.function.Consumer;
009import org.wpilib.annotation.NoDiscard;
010import org.wpilib.units.measure.Time;
011
012/**
013 * Generic interface to represent mechanisms on a robot. Commands can require sole ownership of a
014 * mechanism; when a command that requires a mechanism is running, no other commands may use it at
015 * the same time.
016 *
017 * <p>Even though this interface is named "Mechanism", it may be used to represent other physical
018 * hardware on a robot that should be controlled with commands - for example, an LED strip or a
019 * vision processor that can switch between different pipelines could be represented as mechanisms.
020 *
021 * <p>This class is provided by the Commands v3 VendorDep
022 */
023public interface Mechanism {
024  /**
025   * Returns the scheduler under which this subsystem and its default commands are registered. The
026   * scheduler is also used to fetch running commands for the subsystem.
027   *
028   * @return The registered scheduler.
029   */
030  default Scheduler getRegisteredScheduler() {
031    return Scheduler.getDefault();
032  }
033
034  /**
035   * Marks this mechanism as being controllable when the robot is in a disabled mode. If a mechanism
036   * is not controllable, commands that require it cannot be scheduled when the robot is disabled
037   * and will be canceled when the robot enters a disabled mode.
038   *
039   * <p>By default, mechanisms are not controllable during disabled. Override this method to return
040   * {@code true} if the mechanism should be controllable during disabled modes.
041   *
042   * @return Whether this mechanism is controllable during disabled modes.
043   */
044  default boolean controllableDuringDisabled() {
045    return false;
046  }
047
048  /**
049   * Gets the name of this mechanism. This will default to the name of this mechanism's class.
050   *
051   * @return The name of the mechanism.
052   */
053  @NoDiscard
054  default String getName() {
055    return getClass().getSimpleName();
056  }
057
058  /**
059   * Sets the default command to run on the mechanism when no other command is scheduled. The
060   * default command's priority is effectively the minimum allowable priority for any command
061   * requiring a mechanism. For this reason, it's recommended that a default command have a priority
062   * less than {@link Command#DEFAULT_PRIORITY} so it doesn't prevent low-priority commands from
063   * running.
064   *
065   * <p>The default command is initially an idle command that only owns the mechanism without doing
066   * anything. This command has the lowest possible priority to allow any other command to run.
067   *
068   * @param defaultCommand the new default command
069   */
070  default void setDefaultCommand(Command defaultCommand) {
071    getRegisteredScheduler().setDefaultCommand(this, defaultCommand);
072  }
073
074  /**
075   * Gets the default command that was set by the latest call to {@link
076   * #setDefaultCommand(Command)}.
077   *
078   * @return The currently configured default command
079   */
080  default Command getDefaultCommand() {
081    return getRegisteredScheduler().getDefaultCommandFor(this);
082  }
083
084  /**
085   * Starts building a command that requires this mechanism.
086   *
087   * @param commandBody The main function body of the command.
088   * @return The command builder, for further configuration.
089   */
090  default NeedsNameBuilderStage run(Consumer<Coroutine> commandBody) {
091    return new StagedCommandBuilder().requiring(this).executing(commandBody);
092  }
093
094  /**
095   * Starts building a command that requires this mechanism. The given function will be called
096   * repeatedly in an infinite loop. Useful for building commands that don't need state or multiple
097   * stages of logic.
098   *
099   * @param loopBody The body of the infinite loop.
100   * @return The command builder, for further configuration.
101   */
102  default NeedsNameBuilderStage runRepeatedly(Runnable loopBody) {
103    return run(
104        coroutine -> {
105          while (true) {
106            loopBody.run();
107            coroutine.yield();
108          }
109        });
110  }
111
112  /**
113   * Returns a command that idles this mechanism until another command claims it. The idle command
114   * has {@link Command#LOWEST_PRIORITY the lowest priority} and can be interrupted by any other
115   * command.
116   *
117   * <p>The {@link #getDefaultCommand() default command} for every mechanism is an idle command
118   * unless a different default command has been configured.
119   *
120   * @return A new idle command.
121   */
122  default Command idle() {
123    return run(Coroutine::park).withPriority(Command.LOWEST_PRIORITY).named(getName() + "[IDLE]");
124  }
125
126  /**
127   * Returns a command that idles this mechanism for the given duration of time.
128   *
129   * @param duration How long the mechanism should idle for.
130   * @return A new idle command.
131   */
132  default Command idleFor(Time duration) {
133    return idle().withTimeout(duration);
134  }
135
136  /**
137   * Gets all running commands that require this mechanism. Commands are returned in the order in
138   * which they were scheduled. The returned list is read-only. Every command in the list will have
139   * been scheduled by the previous entry in the list or by intermediate commands that do not
140   * require the mechanism.
141   *
142   * @return The currently running commands that require the mechanism.
143   */
144  @NoDiscard
145  default List<Command> getRunningCommands() {
146    return getRegisteredScheduler().getRunningCommandsFor(this);
147  }
148}
